title: Characterization of the ALDH1A1/MMP11 pathway as a potential biomarker and regulator of prostate cancer progression and metastases
summary:
The CampaMET study aims to investigate the extent to which the presence of certain proteins in the blood of patients with metastatic prostate cancer changes before treatment and after radiation therapy. In addition, tumor cells circulating in the blood will be isolated and examined. 
For this purpose, blood samples already available from participants in previous studies will be used (retrospective part of the study), and patients will be actively asked for their consent for the blood sample collection (prospective part of the study). 
These blood analyses will be used to investigate the potential of certain proteins as possible prognostic biomarkers and regulators of progression and metastasis formation.
conditions: Secondary malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified sites

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Retrospective cohort:
Patients with metastatic prostate cancer who were enrolled in the “Oli-P” study at the trial center of the Clinic and Polyclinic for Radiation Therapy and Radiooncology at the C. G. Carus Dresden University Hospital (EK 194052014, according to the 1st amendment (EK consultation result dated February 2, 2016)), in the “Oli-CR-P” study (EK 194052014, according to the 1st amendment (EK consultation result of February 2, 2016)), the “Oli-CR-P” study (EK 113032019), or the “Poly-CR-P” study defined as the 1st cohort (BO-EK-88022022, according to the 1st amendment (EK consultation result of March 28, 2023)) and from whom blood samples were collected as part of the study until September 30, 2025.

Prospective Cohort:
Patients with metastatic prostate cancer who are being treated for their cancer at the Clinic and Polyclinic for Radiation Therapy and Radio-Oncology at the C. G. Carus University Hospital in Dresden and who give their written consent to the prospective collection of blood samples and data for the present study.
Exclusion criteria:
• age < 18 yrs
• No consent for the use of existing biomaterials and data (retrospective) or for study participation (prospective)
